olivia (support): Forwarding an escalation from Acme internal devs. They see streaming responses cut off on reconnects and occasionally duplicated/partial tokens when clients auto-reconnect. They also reported a sudden billing spike tied to retries. Repro attached by customer below.

raj (eng): ack, can you paste the customer's minimal repro and any server logs? are they on hosted API or Dedicated?

olivia (support): Hosted for now. Customer repro (pasted):
```
# Node client using EventSource polyfill
const es = new EventSource(url + '?stream=true');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('MSG', e.data);
es.onerror = () => { console.log('es error, reconnecting'); es.close(); setTimeout(() => start(), 200); };
```
They say: after reconnect, first chunk is partial (like "Hel" then later "lo world"), sometimes duplicates tokens "worldworld", and sometimes generator returns no further messages.

olivia (support): Server-side logs they pasted: `stream opened 30s`, `stream closed: client reconnect`, `stream resumed, id: none`, `tokens_emitted: 48` then immediately `tokens_emitted: 0` and a retry loop. Also noticed 3x identical requests within 10s.

raj (eng): hmmm. Two hypotheses: 1) client reconnects without resuming last-event-id so server treats it as a fresh request and replays/duplicates tokens. 2) race between stream lifecycle and KV-cache/kv-cache pointer means partial KV state gets lost so server emits partial suffix as new tokens.

kevin (devex): also worth checking the JS SDK's iterator wrapper. We had a regression in the fallback path where EventSource chunk buffering didn't flush on reconnect; the iterator resumed but internal buffer pointer was reset. Might explain partial + duplicate. :bug:

olivia (support): Customer also tried Python generator style and reported empty yields after reconnect:
```
async for chunk in client.stream(...):
    if not chunk: continue
    print(chunk)
```
They see a sequence: 'Hello', '', ' world' (empty string between fragments).

raj (eng): Could you ask for raw SSE frames? We need to see `id:` lines and `data:` chunks. If the reconnect doesn't include `Last-Event-ID` or `id` is missing we'll lose resume point.

olivia (support): Pasted raw frames (customer):
```
event: delta
data: {"tokens":"Hel"}

# reconnect
# new connection has no id header
event: delta
data: {"tokens":"lo"}

# reconnect again
event: delta
data: {"tokens":" world"}
```
They also had occasional frames like `data:` with empty payload.

automod-bot: Automated note: customer reported billing increase by 260% last 24h for stream retries. (reacted :eyes:)

raj (eng): If the server doesn't emit `id:` per event we can't resume deterministically. We need to ensure the runtime attaches stable incremental event ids for SSE resume. Also server should honor `Last-Event-ID` from client.

kevin (devex): On SDK side immediate mitigations: 1) ensure EventSource fallback sends `Last-Event-ID` header when reconnecting (we have code but regression removed it). 2) change iterator to buffer incomplete tokens until newline/marker, don't yield empty strings. 3) make reconnect backoff longer and de-duplicate identical request bodies within short window to avoid billing spikes.

raj (eng): Agreed. Engineering action items:
- attach stable event ids on server stream (eng-runtime)
- verify resume semantics -> server honor Last-Event-ID (eng-runtime)
- patch JS SDK to restore Last-Event-ID behavior and fix buffer pointer (devex)
- patch Python SDK generator to filter empty yields (devex)
- add a short-lived mitigation: server-side idempotency check to drop duplicate requests with same client request-id within 10s (eng-sre)

kevin (devex): I'll open PRs for JS and Python SDKs. Quick patch for JS (concept):
```
// when reconnecting
const lastId = es.lastEventId || localState.lastId;
const urlWithId = new URL(url);
if (lastId) urlWithId.searchParams.set('last_event_id', lastId);
const es2 = new EventSource(urlWithId.toString(), { headers: { 'Last-Event-ID': lastId }});
// iterator: only yield when token.length>0 and buffer complete
```

olivia (support): Customer asked for workaround asap. Suggested temporary steps to them: add jittered reconnect delays, and server advised to avoid simultaneous reconnect attempts from multiple clients. Also we gave them a short client-side dedupe: track last full message hash and ignore immediate duplicates. They implemented and saw fewer duplicates (prelim). :thumbsup:

raj (eng): For the runtime change I'll assign to eng-runtime. We need a small schema: `event id` must be monotonic per connection and persisted in the stream checkpoint. If that's non-trivial, at minimum include a `chunk_index` per response so clients can reassemble.

kevin (devex): Tests to add to repro suite:
- Node EventSource reconnect with missing Last-Event-ID -> expect no duplicate tokens when client supplies last_event_id param
- Python async generator yields no empty chunks on reconnect
- Billing test: rapid reconnect flood should be rate-limited and counted as single session if within dedupe window

olivia (support): I've told the customer we have an engineering investigation and will follow up with timeline. They asked for ETA. Can we give a quick estimate?

raj (eng): I'll triage priority. If we can add event ids and Last-Event-ID handling as a patch, estimate 3-5 business days (small runtime change + test). SDK patches 1-2 days each. SRE mitigation (idempotency drop) 1 day.

kevin (devex): I'll open the JS PR now and reference this thread. PR title: "fix: restore Last-Event-ID on reconnect + buffer pointer fix".

olivia (support): Thanks. I'll keep customer updated. Please ping here when PRs land so I can mark resolved.

raj (eng): tagging owners: @kevin (devex) @olivia (support) @eng-runtime. Next steps logged in ticket. :calendar:
